findings.text: Upheld (Q4, dead path). The diff adds `showsPins`, which ignores its parameter and always returns `true`, so the `if (!showsPins(input)) return null;` branch at contribute.ts:203 can never be taken. The rubric calls 'a flag that is always one value' a dead path and makes any dead path a defect. The spec and plan named this function as a seam while D-9 was still waiting for the person's answer. The person confirmed D-9 on 2026-11-09, so the second branch of the seam is now dead code. The rubric makes no exception for that.

Upheld (Q2, logic duplicated in the diff). The diff adds `knowledgeOn` here and `knowledgeOff` at src/doctor/checks.ts:595. Both load the settings, run `enabledModules(..., BUILT_IN, () => {})` and match `KNOWLEDGE_MODULE`; doctor's copy also takes the long way through BUILT_IN minus the enabled set. This is the same rule, 'is knowledge enabled', written twice, not a repeated line of boilerplate, so it is a defect.
Advisory (Q2, mapping boilerplate): `relate` maps RelateInput to ConsolidateTexts and back, and src/judge/typesafe.ts:77 repeats the same mapping.
Advisory (Q2): KNOWLEDGE_LINE copies the intro, count-line and kind texts from contribute.ts. If that wording changes, echo stripping fails without any error.
Advisory (Q2/Q3): the kind list is declared again here, beside entry.ts's KINDS regex and the OpenCode plugin's copy.
Advisory (Q2): QUOTA hard-codes '20 proposals' instead of using PROPOSALS_PER_HOUR.
Advisory (Q2): the `?? "mcp"` fallback repeats UNKNOWN from src/mcp/agent-id.ts:7. A one-line repeat counts as boilerplate.
Advisory (Q3): whether the payload carries files depends on a wording label (`noun === "memory"`). The name could be sharper.
Advisory (Q3): the log text says 'a version this binary does not support' for every state that is not current, `behind` included. The name does not say the opposite of what the code does.
Advisory (Q5): `pinnedLine` only forwards to `entryLine`.

Advisory (Q2): rebuildAll and refreshOne each repeat the steps that forget a repository, and the freshness comparison is repeated too. These are short repeated statement sequences. Advisory as the reviewer filed it.
Advisory (Q6): searchEntries builds its own placeholders instead of using the file's `placeholders` helper. This is a style difference with the same behaviour.
Advisory (Q6/Q10): rebuildAll's doc comment is stranded above requireKnowledgeRoot's own comment.
Advisory (Q9): the `?? "workspace"` guard covers a case that cannot happen. The reviewer filed it as advisory; the guard hides no traced cause.
Advisory (Q8): `rateKey` is exported but nothing imports it. The rubric calls an unused export advisory.
Advisory (Q4/Q5): the typesafe.tools.* counters are written but no status or doctor line reads them. Each write is reached, so the path is not dead; the counters are just not shown anywhere.
Advisory (Q2): the catch drops checkedAgentId's message and prints the same sentence again. This is a repeated string, not repeated logic.
Advisory (Q11): 'D-9' is cited without '(part 2)', against the ADR's naming convention. No fact, hedge or scope limit is altered.
Advisory (Q1/Q6): the AC-29 assertion accepts either result. A reversion that makes the query throw still fails it, but the test does not show that quoted operators match as words.
Advisory (Q5): EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN runs on the exported constants, not on what the writer executes.
Advisory (Q1): no case fills the candidate limit with higher-ranked hidden entries. Without one, the test does not prove that the confinement happens in SQL rather than after the LIMIT.

Advisory (Q1): the CLI and route cases only check a count of 0; non-zero counts are proven only on compact() itself. The reviewer cited a line of the diff patch (14682), not of the file. The finding is kept as advisory with the file named.
Advisory (Q1): the duplicate-of-proposal refusal is not tested in the target repository or with a stub TypeSafe judge configured. Tests :994 and :1020 cover part of this.
Advisory (Q8): the fixture uses the owner's first name. It names no client.

Advisory: knowledge_propose's body has no maximum length in the schema. The store's checkSize still refuses an oversized body, and the judge's copy is clipped, so nothing oversized is written or sent.

Advisory: by naming itself with different agent ids, a host can spread its calls over 10 rate windows. Part 1's quotas still cap the open proposals, the ADR states that the id is not authenticated, and the id never decides adoption.
Advisory: the 'Known limits of part 2' bullet describes a write that commit cc85251 now refuses (tools.ts:331). The record is out of date, not the code. The session has said it will correct it.

Advisory, not upheld as a defect: this item changes no interface file. Sharing.vue belongs to the sibling item 2026-11-09-002, whose UI/UX gate was ruled in its own round. The console 500 is the failure the capture caused on purpose. The evidence is named only as a bare file name, and there is no review/ui-evidence.json manifest to list it in.
Advisory: copy on the sibling's sharing page, outside this item's change.
Advisory: '1 projects' does not change for a count of one. This is on the sibling's page, outside this item's change.
Advisory: the sharing pill is drawn in the LINKS column. This is on the sibling's page, outside this item's change.
Advisory: the off-switch contrast cannot be measured without axe results. This is on the sibling's page, outside this item's change.
Advisory: the toast covers the sidebar's footer. This is the app's existing toaster position, and the page is the sibling's.
Advisory: the known-limits bullet no longer matches the code (tools.ts:331 refuses the write). Nothing is lost, and the session has said it will correct the record.

Advisory: part 1's limit on a failed module migration needs restating now that migration 7 sits on the hook path. The way back exists (the pre-upgrade backup in openDb), so this is a stale justification, not a failure nobody would see.

Advisory (Q6): spec.md states the dependency on 'parts 1 to 3 ship in one release', so Q5's defect (a dependency the spec does not state) is not met. What is missing is a release step with an owner and an order. The rubric calls a manual step without an owner advisory.

Advisory (Q1): the drain forgets the index rows of a repository whose folder is absent, and logs nothing when it does. The rows are an index that can be rebuilt from the files. A log line per forgotten repository would make this visible.

Advisory (Q4): a wrong 'same' from TypeSafe refuses a proposal. The refusal is handled, logged and returned to the agent, and nothing wrong is written. The cost of tool calls is not shown on any status line.

Upheld (Q1/Q2, a boundary the base draws). CLAUDE.md says everything that reads or writes the knowledge tables goes through the schema gate, and ADR 0024 says a too-new module schema is left alone. Here compact counts and deletes knowledge_shown rows (DELETE at :124) after checking only that the tables exist (`hasShownTables`, :50), never the module's version. A binary at knowledge version 7 would delete rows from a version-8 table. contribute, the tools and doctor all apply the version check. Fix: gate the prune on `moduleSchemaState(...) === "current"`.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it: status reads knowledge tables without checking the module version. It only reads, so it cannot destroy rows the way compact can.
Advisory: the hook path statically loads the store's write-side modules through index-store.ts. Nothing runs at load time, so no stated rule is broken.
Advisory: the MCP transport imports AGENT_ID from the knowledge module by name. The spec's Design names that check, so this follows the Design.
Advisory: rootAreas repeats taxonomyFor's reading of a taxonomy. The Design requires that listing opens no store.
Advisory: KNOWLEDGE_LINE copies contribute.ts's wording. The dependency points the right way (retrieve does not import module code); a test pinning the two together would catch drift.
Advisory: the kind list is repeated outside entry.ts.
Advisory (Q2): pinnedEntries filters `pinned` with no index on it, reaching rows through the primary-key prefix. Bounded; a partial index would make it a seek.
Advisory (Q1): the ADR's reason for rejecting triggers names INSERT OR REPLACE, but the code now deletes the old rows and then does a plain INSERT.
Advisory (Q2): one rate meta row per agent id stays forever. Each is small and holds no personal data.
Advisory (Q2/Q6): rebuildAll's orphan sweep scans the search table. It runs from the CLI only, never on a hook path.
